items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: We didn't call them Portrait's Market Dan, because he'd go around there and help on Portrait's and Rampart's... He'd go around there and help them butchers

ctx.x: Well, I'll ask somebody who lived in that neighborhood.

We didn't call them Portrait's Market Dan, because he'd go around there and help on Portrait's and Rampart's, used to be a public market, it was up at 12 o'clock. He'd go around there and help them butchers, you know, scrape them stands off, and give them a whole lot of meat, you know. You know, meat they didn't think they were going to sell the next day, they'd be going to put in an ice box, they didn't have no refrigerators, they didn't put a hundred pound ice in an ice box, you know, keep that name. Well, he…
a great big bag of stuff, a basket of stuff.
